Two more Fed officials signaled on Thursday they see more hikes ahead, but not of the 50 basis point variety. 

New York Fed President and FOMC vice chair John Williams and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly (2027 voter), traditionally in close alignment with the Fed’s old core of Powell, Jefferson and Williams, both spoke Thursday. As a reminder, Williams, an important voice, has been one of the more dovish members, tipping the October hold ahead of time and later noting that he thought a December hike would be the last under his base case.

▪️ Williams on direction: Inflation is “far too high” and stubbornly persistent, and the Fed still has work to do to get policy to the right place (via Bloomberg). That’s a step up from last week’s more subdued “appropriate time to accumulate more information.”

▪️ Williams on pace: The Fed will need to act “over time.” The economy is resilient and getting stronger but not overheating. He didn’t commit to a specific move in December.

▪️ Daly on direction: “My bias is that further tightening will be needed.” “We have a labor market that’s stable, growth that’s good, but we definitely have an inflation problem right now,” with price pressures spreading into services (via Reuters).

▪️ Daly on pace: Rising bond yields “are most welcome,” and tighter financial conditions give the Fed “a little more time to make really calibrated decisions.” On how much and when: “We have many more pieces of data and information over many, many quarters.”

That makes all 10 Fed officials who’ve spoken on the direction of rates since last Thursday’s selloff lean toward more hikes, but they’re split on how fast. I count four camps:

▪️ Quick, and possibly 50bp: Governor Waller, who said a 50bp hike “should be considered” if core CPI is “around 0.3% or even higher,” and that “hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk.”

▪️ Quicker pace, but not pushing for 50bp: Dallas’ Logan, who sees “at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases” and says “it may be possible to move more rapidly this winter,” and Cleveland’s Hammack, who wants “smaller increments, more frequent, smaller rises.”

▪️ Slower pace: New York’s Williams, the FOMC vice chair (act “over time”); San Francisco’s Daly (“a little more time to make really calibrated decisions”); Philadelphia’s Paulson (“further gradual tightening seems appropriate”); Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman (more tightening “has to be carefully weighed against its costs”); and Richmond’s Barkin (“it is wise to move policy with care”).

▪️ Worried about inflation, but don't want to prejudge decisions: Chicago’s Goolsbee (October CPI was “borderline disturbing”) and St. Louis’ Musalem (inflation is “a regressive tax”).

Among the six December voters who’ve weighed in, that’s one for quick and possibly 50bp, two for quicker quarter-point steps and three, including the FOMC vice chair, for a more measured pace. 

That makes 25bp in December the base case, with the real debate over how quickly the next hikes follow which will be teased out in the dot plot. October PCE and November payrolls, both out before the Dec. 8–9 meeting, will be key.

It feels like a BTC confidence crash not a price one.

For vibe-memecoins like BTC, price is the product and the lower the price goes the weaker the belief in it's SoV story.

The current dump is especially painful as many believed $58k was the bottom and failure to retrace while AI stocks bounce backed hurt badly.

So BTC continues to dump without significant dip buyers who end up buying AI crash than crypto.

Obviously, if BTC drops significantly lower the dip buyers will appear chasing a bounce back.

But those might be short-term traders instead of buying for long-term hold.

Previously, on dips like this CT would be full with bull-posters sharing their sound-money thesis with perhaps too delusional takes. They lifted the spirits.

Now it's All Quiet on the Western Front

Based from ppl I talk to and on sentiment on X, BTC simply isn't as exciting as it used to be.

Previously BTC maxis are selling some BTC for ZEC or even PRL as a hedge if BTC fails.

BTC FAILURE WAS NOT AN OPTION FOR OG MAXIS! That is the confidence shake up I feel.

And with ETFs BTC is becoming like a 'boomer' coin but without boomers actually significantly allocating to it (judging from ETF flows).

Worrying are stablecoin outflows, MSTR excluded from MSCI. The lower the BTC goes, the stronger the MSTR FUD will get.

I'd say the confidence crisis is more applicable to BTC as alts are holding surprisingly well vs BTC. The pet-rock just drags everything down.

Crypto still has a long road of adoption ahead of us: don't forget about recent HYPE and AVAX partnerships.

But these partnerships have little to do with BTC as BTC isn't a great trade for overall crypto adoption anymore.

So I wish other alts stopped trading with BTC on the way down as well.

Hope I'm wrong and my bearish bias is talking here and X algo just fails to show bullish posts to me.

Looking for your -non AI- counter arguments in the comments.

Just to state the nuances of my opinion: Jensen is irreplaceable to $NVDA.

No other CEO can visit a chicken shop in Korea, noodle shop in Japan

And rally hundred of billions of capital and supply chain commitment into Nvidia’s next technological vision.

That Nvidia could compound 70% capacity constrained growth Y/Y, without a leader like Jensen making these transformational bets.

- I expect some potential slowdown in Nvidia’s ecosystem.

I don’t think an accountant can make the same aggressive level of commitments to Neoclouds or supply chains in Taiwan, Korea, Japan beyond existing architectures.

Then rally the capital and trust to make it happen.

- I do expect the next CEO to be more politically aligned with Washington in restricting China GPU access

- I also see the next CEO being less supportive of open weight models (positive for OpenAI/Anthropic)

- I’m less optimistic on $NVDA maintaining their competitive advantages against $AMD, $AVGO, and hyperscalers.

One person doesn’t break the AI trade, I expect companies from optics to memory to still outperform.

However, my confidence in the next leg of Nvidia’s growth, beyond their current roadmap, has been shaken without Jensen Huang.

Film it side on next time for us mate. 

It looks okay but probably a bit high based on this angle. But yeh don’t think much valuable feedback from here 

Only comments would be you’re not bracing as well as you could be hence the slight movements on your way up / between reps. Drawing down the ribs with chest up is very useful cue for me before unracking and broadly just having a tighter setup across your back via a slightly narrower grip. 

Equally some small ankle collapse on the way down, my suspicion is from being 1-2 inches too wide with your foot placement but that’s just me guessing as you jump your feet out right before the first rep and at heavier weights combining this all together could lead to knee collapse, some ankle rotation, lack of core stability from bracing and leaving a lot of power output in the tank. 

My advice would be 1. Film a new angle 2. Work on your setup getting tighter across your back, through your core and play around slightly with foot placement (could be wrong on this one it’s just at a glance I think it doesn’t look super comfortable for you). Most of this is resolved before you even do a rep. 

Think you can probably move a lot more weight once you improve this, and if depth is an issue - would look into some ankle and hip mobility drills to do alongside your squat work 

All that said - it doesn’t look bad man these are all bits of advice I think may help you move more weight in a more controlled way - the strength is there imo

You need to get very comfortable with boredom when investing

You cannot do well if you want to feel excitement 

By definition investment is long term and if you expect to feel excited and thrilled you are the 99% of people who end up buying high and selling low and you become the old man who said “I use to own X”

Most people have so little patience that 2 yrs of owning something feels like eternity when that is actually short 

All the great investments span decades

To get exceptional returns you must do what others don’t by definition - out holding others long term through thick and thin - excitement and boredom is one of the parts to it as long as the grand long term arc is still in place
